text:
Dylan Larkin is a Canadien now, and Detroit has not missed a beat on the scoreboard. In the first game after the trade ended his standoff with the club, Red Wings fans chanted "who needs Larkin" during a 5-1 win over Vancouver, and the team followed it with a 2-0 shutout in Columbus last night behind John Gibson's 18 saves. That is a cheerful week for a team sitting on 23 points with a 16% chance at the playoffs by our simulations. The catch is in the chances: Detroit had only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) across its last five games and still went 3-2. Moritz Seider is embracing what Sports Illustrated called a new era, and Emmitt Finnie, with three points against the Canucks, is the young name getting written about.

Daniil Tarasov is the main reason the results have held. He is at a .930 save rate and 11.6 goals saved above expected this season, after finishing 2.8 below expected a year ago, and he is .933 over his last five starts. Andreas Englund faces Nashville for the first time since leaving, and Viktor Arvidsson gets his old team too, fresh off a three-point night.

Nashville arrives off a 6-5 shootout loss to Utah in which it blew a two-goal lead. The Predators' last five tell a stranger story than their 2-2-1 record: they had 53% of the expected goals, won the chance battle in Dallas by a wide margin and were badly outplayed by Utah. Filip Forsberg has a five-game point streak and Steven Stamkos is closing in on a milestone, according to Yahoo Sports. Jonathan Marchessault has three points in two games since coming back from injury.

Both teams played last night, which our numbers account for. Justus Annunen starts for Nashville over Juuse Saros, who has 19 of the 25 starts, and Annunen is at .863 and 2.1 goals below expected in seven games. Our numbers see this one as close to even on chances: Nashville at 47% of five-on-five expected goals this season, Detroit at 48%.
headline: Life after Larkin looks oddly cheerful in Detroit
